transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
Ukraine says the satellite communication system that guides its drones
has been placed under crippling restrictions.
The Trump administration controls that satellite system
and has warned it could scale back intelligence sharing.
Here's NPR's Greg Myrie.
Ukraine says when its drones exceed at 100 miles per hour,
which they routinely do, the communication signal was cut,
rendering the drones useless.
Ukraine's military uses something called Star Shield,
the military version of a network that comes from the much better-known
civilian system Starlink, which is headed by Elon Musk.
Musk says on social media the U.S. government controls Star Shield
and any restrictions would have been done by the U.S. military or President Trump.
Neither Trump nor the military has commented,
but the president has been telling Ukraine to stop attacking
Russian oil facilities.
U.S. officials have also warned that intelligence cooperation could be halted.
Greg Myrie, NPR News, Washington.
President Trump has wrapped up a midterm campaign swing
through western states in Montana.
The rally in Kalispell, outside Glacier National Park,
was his second of the day.
And Arizona, Trump defended the airplane he's using as Air Force One,
opening his remarks by describing how the jet was a gift from the Qatar royal family.
Inflation worsened last month.
Labor departments as the consumer price index rose 3.7 percent in September,
compared with a year ago, up from 3.4 percent in August.
Here's NPR's Scott Horsley.
Average wages have gone up just 3 percent over the last year,
while prices have jumped 3.7 percent.
So that means the typical paycheck buys less today than it did a year ago.
And no wonder many workers feel like they're falling behind.
It's a little different for retirees.
We got word that social security benefits will go up 3.6 percent in January.
That's an automatic cost of living adjustment, or COLA,
that's supposed to protect seniors from inflation.
A spike in gasoline prices tied to the war with Iran accounts for more than half the monthly increase.
Pope Leo up and walking following surgery that confirmed he has lung cancer.
Doctors say his recovery is proceeding as planned.
From Rome, Megan Williams reports.
The Vatican says the 71-year-old pope is recovering as expected after Tuesday's operation.
He's walking around his hospital room doing respiratory therapy and eating normally.
Surgeons removed the lower lobe of his right lung after tests confirmed adenocarcinoma,
the most common form of lung cancer.
Doctors say there were no complications from the surgery, which lasted around 90 minutes.
They're now waiting for further tests to show whether the cancer had spread
and whether Leo will need additional treatment.
For NPR News, I'm Megan Williams in Rome.
And you're listening to NPR News.
Iran-backed Houthi rebels have attacked the headquarters of the Saudi oil company Aramco.
Officials say offices of senior executives were damaged.
The strikes are part of intensifying attacks on Saudi Arabia by the Houthis and neighboring Yemen.
AI is often associated with replacing white-collar jobs and even destroying humanity.
But in India, AI is being developed to replace industrial jobs.
NPR's Diya Hadid reports on factory workers who are training their own replacements.
In a textile factory in the southern Indian town of Karur, women pack aprons into plastic packaging
and record their every hand movement through a GoPro fussened on a headset.
That footage is called egocentric data.
Developers need millions of hours of it to train AI robots.
Even as experts say India is emerging as a key place to record egocentric data,
they say the development of AI robots will likely be deployed in countries where labor is more expensive
and power is cheaper.
They say these women in factory jobs might be saved by the fact that their labor is cheap,
most are paid around $100 a month, and power here is considered expensive.
For now, Diya Hadid, NPR News, Karur, Tamil Nadu, India.
The financial markets in Asia are falling sharply in Thursday trading.
South Korea's benchmark down more than 7 percent.
And Japan's Nikkei has slipped 4.5 percent amid a deepening sell-off in technology shares.
The losses in Asia follows Wednesday decline on Wall Street
after the government said inflation worsened in September.
I'm Giles Snyder, NPR News.
Before you renew your car insurance policy, download the Jerry app or head to jerry.ai/npr.

topics.text: Ukraine says US-controlled Starlink-based Star Shield restrictions cut drone guidance signals, rendering them useless
Trump wraps midterm campaign swing through western states, rallying in Kalispell, Montana
September consumer price index rises 3.7 percent year over year, with gasoline spike tied to Iran war
Pope Leo recovering after lung surgery confirming adenocarcinoma, doctors report no complications
Houthi rebels attack Saudi oil company Aramco headquarters, damaging executive offices
India textile workers record hand movements to train AI robots that may replace them
Asian stock markets sharply fall Thursday, South Korea down over 7 percent, Japan's Nikkei down 4.5 percent
